# VAYU — full description

> VAYU (https://vayuai.vercel.app) is a hyper-local air pollution and anomaly detection platform for Kolkata and India, built by team Doomsday for the Google Cloud hackathon, Track 2: CleanAir & Clear Streets.

## The problem

City-wide air quality apps rely on a few sparse monitoring stations. They miss street-level events such as garbage fires, industrial smoke or heavy local congestion.

## How VAYU works

1. Citizen reports — residents photograph smoke, burning waste or dust. Gemini Vision returns a structured verdict: smoke/dust detected, pollution type, severity 0–10, estimated AQI impact and confidence. The report is stored with its GPS location.
2. IoT sensors — Arduino Uno + ESP8266 nodes with an MQ135 gas sensor and a TMP36 temperature sensor post readings over HTTPS.
3. Satellite data — current and hourly US AQI from Copernicus CAMS (via Open-Meteo) for the visitor's location, plus reference stations at Kolkata centre, Salt Lake, Bhowanipore and Howrah.
4. Fusion — readings from the last 30 minutes are grouped into ~500 m grid cells. Gemini decides whether each cell is a hotspot, its severity, a 24-hour AQI prediction and the recommended municipal action. Hotspots are stored in Google BigQuery.
5. Act — confirmed hotspots are listed by severity with exact coordinates and the recommended action. A municipal officer can send an SMS or WhatsApp alert (Hindi, English or both) through Twilio. Every alert is logged.

## Pages and sections

- Home (/#home): greeting, location, current temperature and weather, current AQI with category, next 5 days
- Report (/#report): photo upload or camera capture, voice description, Gemini Vision result
- Detect (/#detect): temperature, AQI and hotspot counts; AQI chart for past hours and the next 24 hours; hotspot map; Gemini analysis and "Run Hotspot Detection"
- Act (/#act): top confirmed hotspots with directions and alert dispatch; count of alerts sent
- FAQ (/#faq)
- Team (/#team)
- Live map (/map)

## AQI categories used

Good 0–50 · Satisfactory 51–100 · Moderate 101–200 · Poor 201–300 · Very poor 301–400 · Severe 401+

## Frequently asked questions

Q: What is VAYU?
A: A neighbourhood-level air pollution map for India that combines citizen photo reports, low-cost IoT sensors and satellite air-quality data, using Google Gemini AI to find pollution hotspots street by street.

Q: How do I report pollution in my area?
A: Open the Report section, take a photo of the smoke, burning waste or dust, allow location access and submit. Gemini Vision analyses it within seconds and adds it to the hotspot map.

Q: Where does the air quality data come from?
A: Satellite-derived data from Copernicus CAMS via Open-Meteo, on the US AQI scale, plus VAYU sensor nodes and citizen reports when available.

Q: Which areas does VAYU cover?
A: It was built in West Bengal with its first stations around Kolkata, Salt Lake, Bhowanipore and Howrah. Live AQI, weather and forecasts work anywhere in India.

Q: What happens after a hotspot is detected?
A: It appears in the Act section with location, severity and a recommended action, and a municipal officer can dispatch an SMS or WhatsApp alert in one tap.

Q: Who built VAYU?
A: Team Doomsday: Chanchal Pradhan (backend), Partha Biswas (UI/UX and hardware), Ankit Gupta (frontend) and Sumit Mandi (machine learning).

Q: Which languages does VAYU support?
A: English, Hindi, Bengali, Odia, Gujarati, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Punjabi and Assamese.

## Technology

Next.js on Vercel · Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (vision and text) · Google BigQuery · Firebase Storage · Google Maps JavaScript API · Open-Meteo · Twilio · Arduino Uno + ESP8266, MQ135, TMP36
